name: Two Walks and Progressive Link
notes: Owner's description (2026-11-16): walk forward slow, slow; then quick, quick into promenade. Slow 1: the lead walks forward on his left; slow 2: forward on his right. Quick 1: a wide step taking weight on the left, opening into promenade as he steps. Quick 2: weight back onto the right with no travel (the owner turns the right foot slightly, ready for the promenade; the model has no foot direction separate from the body, so that twist isn't shown). The follow mirrors: back on her right, back on her left, a wide step on her right, weight back onto her left. Named after the standard figures: two Walks and a Progressive Link. In the book the link's first quick is a small step forward and its second a step side and slightly back; the owner's version steps wide on the first quick and changes weight back on the second, ending in the same place: the lead on his right, his left foot out along the line of travel. Provisional (owner accepted the waltz sizes as a starting point): walks 0.5 each, straight (real tango walks curve gradually left); the wide step lands level with the other foot and 0.4 out from where it was, so the feet end 0.6 apart; the opening is an eighth each (the lead turning left, the follow right, as in the waltz promenade) and happens on quick 1; no rise (tango has none); closed hold is the same as the waltz's, the follow offset 0.1 to the lead's right (2026-11-17), though real tango's offset is larger. Timing: 2/4, a slow is one beat and a quick half. Ends in the "tango promenade" stance (feet apart and uncrossed, owner's description; the V open to the lead's left), with the lead's right foot 1.0 forward and 0.1 right of where the midpoint of his feet started.
